clue.text: Curry gets cold, very cold

parts.note: a balti is a type of curry cooked in a metal pan
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A curry that has gone cold is a disappointment, made worse by icy conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: A balti is a curry dish popular in Britain. 'cold' appears twice: once as the letter C and once inside the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Baltic, used informally, describes freezing weather, after the chilly sea of that name.

clue.text: A very soft, extremely large type of fruit

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very soft

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its outer letters, here the ends of large

parts.note: first and last letters

explanation.surface: A huge, very squashy fruit is described.
explanation.definitionFit: An apple is a common fruit grown on trees in orchards.

clue.text: Worked out tons, then showered

parts.note: to shower is to rain lightly

explanation.surface: After a heavy workout at the gym, someone took a shower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worked out' and 'showered' paint a gym visit; 'showered' is the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Trained means exercised, as an athlete does in the gym.

clue.text: Piece of lettuce put over piece of meat?

indicators.note: in a down clue, put over means turned upside down, so the letters read backwards
a piece of the word is a run of its letters, here inside lettuce

parts.note: the run of letters sits inside the word

explanation.surface: A leaf of salad placed on top of a slice of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut is a portion of meat taken from a particular part of the animal, such as a brisket.

clue.text: Abandon attempt after warning cry

indicators.note: after puts the attempt piece behind the warning cry piece in the answer

parts.note: fore is the shout golfers give to warn people of an incoming ball
a go is a try or attempt

explanation.surface: Someone gives up a try after hearing somebody shout a warning.
explanation.walkthrough: FORE is shouted on a golf course to warn of a flying ball.
explanation.definitionFit: To forego something is to give it up or do without it, a synonym of abandon.

clue.text: Excellent tart cooked with fries

indicators.note: cooked suggests ingredients being worked over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fine pastry is served alongside chips.
explanation.definitionFit: First-rate means of the highest class or quality, top-notch.

clue.text: One who regrets taking in Liberal leader

indicators.note: taking in means absorbing, so the liberal letter goes inside

parts.note: to rue is to regret, so one who rues is a ruer

explanation.surface: A remorseful person welcomes the head of the Liberal party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal leader' looks like it means just the letter L, but 'leader' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler is a sovereign or head of state, someone who governs and leads.

clue.text: Medicinal root in spirits (English)

parts.note: gins are spirits

explanation.surface: A healing plant root is found in English alcoholic drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginseng is a plant root used in herbal remedies as a tonic.

clue.text: Drop liquid on middle of massive dish

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its centre letter, here taken from massive

parts.note: the central letter of the seven-letter word massive
a platter is a large serving dish

explanation.surface: Someone spills liquid onto the centre of an enormous serving dish.
explanation.definitionFit: To splatter is to splash or spray liquid in drops over something.

clue.text: Flooring somewhat useful in outhouses

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A type of floor covering is fairly practical in garden sheds.
explanation.definitionFit: Lino, short for linoleum, is a hard-wearing floor covering.

clue.text: Adolescent requiring support with last bit of revision

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball before it is struck

indicators.note: the final letter of the word revision is taken

parts.note: its final letter

explanation.surface: A teenager needs help with the end of their exam revision.
explanation.definitionFit: A teen is a young person in their teenage years, an adolescent.

clue.text: Tenner stupidly invested in IT and computer network

indicators.note: invested in means placed inside, so the rearranged letters go within IT
doing something stupidly mixes it up, so the letters of tenner are rearranged

explanation.surface: A ten-pound note was foolishly sunk into information technology and a computer network.
explanation.walkthrough: A tenner is British slang for a ten-pound note; 'invested' fits the money story but here means placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The internet is the worldwide system linking computers together, a global network.

clue.text: Start eating, it's falling apart!

indicators.note: falling apart means breaking into pieces, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tucks into a meal that collapses.
explanation.definitionFit: To instigate something is to bring it about or set it going, to initiate.

clue.text: A dreadful barber's not in agreement

parts.note: Sweeney Todd is the murderous barber of Fleet Street, so a dreadful barber's is Todd's

explanation.surface: Someone describes a terrible hairdresser's shop as one where people disagree.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweeney Todd is the demon barber of Victorian melodrama and the Sondheim musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at odds means being in conflict or disagreement with someone.

clue.text: Odd characters from the day trip meet when drinks are served

indicators.note: odd characters are the first, third, fifth letters and so on of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Peculiar people on the outing gather when refreshments come round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd characters' suggests eccentric people; here it means the odd-numbered letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Teatime is the late-afternoon hour when tea, the British drink, is taken.

clue.text: When transgression overwhelms key delegate

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: overwhelms means engulfs, so the transgression piece goes around the key

parts.note: a sin is a transgression or wrongdoing
G is a musical key

explanation.surface: Wrongdoing takes control of the main representative sent on someone's behalf.
explanation.definitionFit: To assign a task is to delegate or allot it to another person.

clue.text: Least hard questions at the end of exam

indicators.note: at the end picks the final letter of questions

parts.note: its last letter
a test is an exam

explanation.surface: The easiest questions come at the end of the exam.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'questions' and 'exam' look like TEST; only 'exam' is, and 'at the end' takes the last letter of 'questions'.
explanation.definitionFit: Softest is the superlative of soft, the opposite of hardest.

clue.text: Heaven is going into lots of shops

indicators.note: going into means entering, so is is placed inside the row of shops

parts.note: a parade is a row of shops along a street

explanation.surface: Bliss is visiting a whole lot of stores, according to the shopper.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a parade is a short row of shops.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise is the abode of the blessed, another name for heaven.

clue.text: Accomplished head of admin department

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here from admin

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: A skilled manager runs the administration office.
explanation.definitionFit: Adept means skilful and expert, as accomplished does.

clue.text: Energy contained in the majority of rich food

indicators.note: contained in means held within, so the energy letter goes inside the shortened word
the majority of a word is all but its last letter

parts.note: full can mean rich, as in a full-bodied flavour
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Calories lie within most rich food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Energy' looks like the definition, but it supplies E, which goes inside FUL (FULL with its last letter dropped by 'the majority of').
explanation.definitionFit: Food is the fuel the body burns, so the two words share the sense of nourishment that powers you.

clue.text: Be dangerous, ultimately blocking the way out

indicators.note: blocking means obstructing, so the letter sits inside the exit

parts.note: an exit is the way out

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letter of dangerous is taken

parts.note: its last letter

explanation.surface: It is risky to obstruct a fire exit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be dangerous' reads as one phrase, but 'Be' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To exist is to have being, so it can stand in for the verb be.

clue.text: Father beginning to seethe with anger

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, here from seethe

parts.note: its first letter
ire is anger

explanation.surface: A dad starts to boil with fury.
explanation.definitionFit: A sire is a male parent, especially of a horse, or an old word for a father.

clue.text: Strong, lithe cat jumping about

indicators.note: jumping about suggests leaping around in disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A supple feline leaps around energetically.
explanation.definitionFit: An athletic person is fit and physically powerful, a sense of strong.

clue.text: Trendy hotel — one with parking

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
I is the Roman numeral one
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A fashionable hotel that offers a car park.
explanation.definitionFit: Hip is slang for fashionable and up to date.

clue.text: Courage shown by copper, perhaps, according to report

indicators.note: according to report means as it is heard said, so the word is one that sounds like another

parts.note: copper is an example of a metal

explanation.surface: Bravery displayed by a police officer, perhaps, as the news says.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a police officer; here it is the metal, and 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Mettle is a person's spirit and resilience, their capacity to face difficulty bravely.

clue.text: Vegetable dish with occasional chunks of ham, too

parts.note: a pot is a cooking dish

indicators.note: occasional means every other one, so alternate letters are taken

parts.note: alternate letters, starting from the second

explanation.surface: A vegetable dish also has some bits of ham in it.
